A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCDS study and contain the main text, references, and Appendices A-G. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original SCDS evaluations on LASA and Robomimic, robot simulations, sensitivity analyses, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, simulation, and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Sections 2-3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same REN dynamics, linear projection, coupling layers, initialization, trajectory losses, and optimization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LASA-2D/4D, Robomimic-6D/14D, Snake motions, and Isaac Lab manipulation/navigation scenarios. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: SNDS, SDS-EF, and BC remain the evaluated baselines in the corresponding benchmark and timing comparisons. The appendix ablation comparators are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The OOS initial-state sampling procedures, MSE and soft-DTW metrics, demonstration splits, model configurations, and training/evaluation settings match throughout Section 5 and Appendices E-G.

E4.justification: Appendix E retains the same contraction-rate and latent-dimension analyses, bijective-layer and REN-to-RNN ablations, and recovery tests from increasingly distant initial states.

E5.justification: The existing ± reporting, plotted uncertainty bands, and Table 4's 50-trial statement are unchanged. No seed, repetition, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings match, including all appendix results. For example, Table 1 retains SCDS OOS MSE of 0.32 ± 0.15 on LASA-2D and 2.68 ± 0.65 on Robomimic-14D.

T1.justification: The contraction definition, Proposition 2.1, Assumption 4.1, Theorem 4.1, Corollary 4.1.1, and mathematical material in Appendices A and D are unchanged. Footnote renumbering does not alter the arguments.

C1.justification: The revised abstract preserves the same claims about contractive policies, unconstrained learning, OOS loss bounds, and simulated performance. The introduction's contributions and Section 6 conclusions retain their scope.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of OOS recovery, contraction-versus-expressivity tradeoffs, and computational costs. The longer-horizon limitation and future-work discussion in Section 6 are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F and Tables 6-7 retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and code references. The identical project URL moves from an introduction footnote to the abstract; no resource-availability change is reported.

R1.justification: The references and related-work discussions in Section 1 and Appendix B are unchanged, including the positioning against existing stable and contractive imitation methods.

P1.justification: v2 corrects the abstract's 'using modeled' wording, lightly rewrites its closing sentences, relocates the project link, and makes small introduction and caption edits. It also updates the funding acknowledgment; section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ICLR 2025 publication header and introduces minor first-page reflow and footnote changes. Figures 1-21 and Tables 1-7 retain their visual content and structure, with small wording edits to the captions of Figures 6 and 7.

improvement.justification: The abstract is slightly cleaner and the existing project link more prominent, but the method, theoretical arguments, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, including the appendices. These limited editorial and publication-format updates leave overall paper quality essentially the same.
